taxonomic_note: Accepted by current Kew/POWO with two accepted varieties, var. triflorus and var. integrifolius. The learner stays species-level; staminode hairiness varies among the varieties.
look_here_first: Start with the glossy leaves and the narrower pink-to-red corolla. Hill Country penstemon is an erect perennial with opposite dark-green leaves; lower leaves are often toothed while upper leaves become smaller and more entire/connate. Flowers are usually about 25–35 mm, distinctly smaller than P. cobaea.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Hays County — TPWD/TxDOT county rare-species documentation explicitly lists threeflower penstemon for Hays County. Kerr County — the Kerr Wildlife Management Area vascular flora lists Penstemon triflorus; multiple herbarium collections also document it near Kerrville. Bandera County — University of Colorado herbarium records include a Texas, Bandera County specimen of Penstemon triflorus.
project_inclusion.range_guardrail: Cultivated/display records from the Lady Bird Johnson Wildflower Center in Travis County are not counted; Texas Wildbuds explicitly notes those plants are not native to Travis County.

best_field_traits: perennial with several erect to bushy stems
upper leaves smaller and often entire/connate
corolla usually about 25–35 mm and pink/rose/red to lavender depending variety
pale throat commonly marked with darker guide lines
staminode glabrous in var. triflorus but lightly bearded in var. integrifolius
morphology_keys.comparison_training: Penstemon cobaea: P. cobaea has much larger 35–55 mm pale flowers with a strongly inflated throat and broader serrate leaves. Penstemon baccharifolius: P. baccharifolius is a woody-based low subshrub with thick leathery serrate leaves and red flowers from cliff/rock crevices. Penstemon tenuis: P. tenuis has tiny 10–14 mm lavender flowers, sharp small calyx lobes and a wetter coastal/alluvial ecology.
